title: Epp field hypothesis for complete local domains
statement: Let $p$ be prime, let $k_0$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p$, and let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a complete Noetherian local integral domain of characteristic $p$ with an inclusion $k_0\hookrightarrow R$ [def-weil-field], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Local means that $\mathfrak m$ is the unique maximal ideal, and integral domain means $1\ne0$ and no zero divisors. For any field $E$ of characteristic $p$, put $E_{\mathrm{perf}}=\bigcap_{n\geq0}E^{p^n}$, where $E^{p^n}=\{x^{p^n}:x\in E\}$; this is its maximal perfect subfield. A field is perfect here if $x\mapsto x^p$ is surjective. Put $k=R/\mathfrak m$ and $F=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, the field of fractions of $R$. If every element of $k_{\mathrm{perf}}$ is algebraic over the image of $k_0$ in $k$, then every element of $F_{\mathrm{perf}}$ is algebraic over $k_0\subset F$. Algebraic means satisfying a nonzero polynomial over that field.

source.place: Expose IV 3.2.1 and Proposition 3.2.3(i),(iv), as applied in 4.2.3; the coefficient-field form (iv), together with Cohen structure, applies compatibly with the specified perfect subfield.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-domain-finite-over-regular] to $R$. It gives a subring $A\subseteq R$, finite as a module extension, with the same residue field and an isomorphism $A\simeq C[[t_1,\ldots,t_d]]$ for a coefficient field $C$. The alternative coefficient Cohen ring is impossible: by the cited statement its maximal ideal is generated by a prime integer, whereas in characteristic $p$ that integer is either zero or a unit, so cannot generate the proper nonzero maximal ideal of a discrete valuation ring. In a formal power series ring over $C$, the constant-coefficient map has kernel the zero-constant series; any series with nonzero constant coefficient is inverted by a geometric series, computed degree by degree [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Thus its residue field is $C$. Write $s:k\to C\subseteq R$ for the inverse of the residue isomorphism on constants. Constants identify $C$ with $k$; no assertion about compatibility with $k_0$ has yet been used.

source.place: IV 3.2.3(iv), Cohen structure; Stacks Tag 032D, label lemma-complete-local-Noetherian-domain-finite-over-regular, equal-characteristic case

proof.text: The section $s$ preserves the specified $k_0$. For $a\in k_0$ and every $n$, choose $a_n\in k_0$ with $a_n^{p^n}=a$. Then $s(\overline{a_n})-a_n\in\mathfrak m$ and, by the characteristic-$p$ binomial identity, $s(\bar a)-a=(s(\overline{a_n})-a_n)^{p^n}\in\mathfrak m^{p^n}$. Completeness includes $\bigcap_r\mathfrak m^r=0$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]; the exponents $p^n$ are cofinal in the natural numbers, so $s(\bar a)=a$. Thus $k_0\subseteq C$ is precisely the given inclusion into $R$. The residue isomorphism identifies $C_{\mathrm{perf}}$ with $k_{\mathrm{perf}}$, since it and its inverse commute with every $p^n$-th power. Hence every element of $C_{\mathrm{perf}}$ is algebraic over this $k_0$.

source.place: IV 3.2.3(iv) as used in IV 4.2.3; compatibility of coefficient representatives with a perfect subfield

proof.text: Put $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. Localize a finite $A$-module generating set of $R$ at $A\setminus\{0\}$: its images span $B=(A\setminus\{0\})^{-1}R$ as a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space. Since $R$ is a domain and $A\subseteq R$, $B$ is a domain. For $0\ne b\in B$, multiplication by $b$ is an injective linear endomorphism of this finite-dimensional space, hence surjective; some $c$ satisfies $bc=1$. Thus $B$ is a field containing $R$, and every fraction of elements of $R$ lies in $B$. Conversely $B$ already consists of such fractions. Therefore $B=F$ and $F/K$ is finite.

source.place: IV 3.2.3(iv), passage from the finite Cohen parameter ring to fraction fields

proof.text: For any characteristic-$p$ field $H$, compute in the Laurent series ring $H((t))$ [def-weil-pbc-laurent-series]. This is a field: a nonzero series is $a t^r(1+u)$ with $a\ne0$ and $u\in tH[[t]]$, and its inverse is $a^{-1}t^{-r}\sum_{j\ge0}(-u)^j$; each coefficient is a finite sum, and multiplication telescopes. For $q=p^n$, the coefficient formula is $(\sum_i b_i t^i)^q=\sum_i b_i^q t^{qi}$. Indeed, shift to a power series, truncate at any fixed degree, and apply the finite characteristic-$p$ binomial identity; discarded terms cannot affect that degree. If $z$ has a $q$-th root for every $n$, every exponent in its support is divisible by all $p^n$, hence is zero. It is a constant $c$, and the same coefficient formula shows $c=b_0^{p^n}$ in $H$ for every $n$. Conversely, roots in $H$ give constant roots in $H((t))$. Thus $H((t))_{\mathrm{perf}}=H_{\mathrm{perf}}$ as constant subfields, including $z=0$.

Set $L_0=C$ and $L_i=L_{i-1}((t_i))$ for $1\leq i\leq d$. Group a multivariate power series by the exponent of $t_d$, then recursively by $t_{d-1},\ldots,t_1$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. This gives an injective homomorphism $A\to L_d$: equality is coefficientwise, and multiplication agrees because each fixed multidegree has finitely many decompositions. Since $L_d$ is a field by the preceding step, the map extends to $K$ by $a/b\mapsto a b^{-1}$; cross multiplication verifies well-definedness and injectivity. Every element of $K_{\mathrm{perf}}$ therefore lies in $(L_d)_{\mathrm{perf}}=C_{\mathrm{perf}}$, applying the preceding calculation $d$ times. Conversely $C_{\mathrm{perf}}\subseteq K_{\mathrm{perf}}$ because its roots in $C$ are constants in $K$. Consequently $K_{\mathrm{perf}}=C_{\mathrm{perf}}$. For $d=0$ the embedding and this equality are the identities on $C$.

source.place: IV 3.2.3(iii), induction using iterated Laurent series

proof.text: The extension $F/K$ is finite by step 3 and both fields have characteristic $p$. Apply [lem-per-finite-extension-perfect-core]. Every $x\in F_{\mathrm{perf}}$ is algebraic over $K_{\mathrm{perf}}=C_{\mathrm{perf}}$. This application includes inseparable finite extensions; no generic separability of the Cohen parameter map is assumed.

Fix $x\in F_{\mathrm{perf}}$ and take a monic polynomial $T^r+c_{r-1}T^{r-1}+\cdots+c_0$ over $C_{\mathrm{perf}}$ annihilating $x$; divide a nonzero annihilating polynomial by its leading coefficient. Each $c_i$ is algebraic over $k_0$ by step 2. Choose a monic polynomial of degree $e_i$ over $k_0$ for each $c_i$. Reducing powers by these equations and by the equation for $x$ shows that $k_0[c_0,\ldots,c_{r-1},x]$ is spanned over $k_0$ by the finitely many monomials $c_0^{a_0}\cdots c_{r-1}^{a_{r-1}}x^b$ with $0\leq a_i<e_i$ and $0\leq b<r$. More powers of $x$ than the size of this spanning set are linearly dependent over $k_0$, producing a nonzero polynomial over $k_0$ annihilating $x$. This is the desired algebraicity for every $x$, with $x=0$ covered by $T$.

source.place: IV 3.2.3(i),(iv), final algebraicity transitivity written on finitely many coefficients

proof_origin.place: Expose IV 3.2.2–3.2.3, especially (iii),(iv), and application IV 4.2.3; Cohen structure input from Stacks Tag 032D.
